items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I had the old man, Umprey. Willie Umprey, the clarinet player, yeah. And I had a Mani Manetta on the piano, and I was playing guitar... we only had five pieces.

ctx.x: Yeah, that was my job. I had Mani Manetta. Who else did you? I had the old man, Umprey. Willie Umprey, the clarinet player, yeah. And I had a Mani Manetta on the piano, and I was playing guitar. That time I was playing guitar. And John Vino on the drum. And... Let's see, we only had five pieces. See, I count five. Mani Manetta, Willie Umprey, John Vino, myself, and the piano.
Did you have a carnet in those days?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I was in 19, say 1920, at Fortify... I had old man Willie Umprey on the clarinet.

ctx.x: I was in 19, say 1920, at Fortify. And, uh, Manetto was on the piano and I was playing guitar. John Veen on the drum. And, uh, Tinette on the violin. We didn't have no trumpet, no. I had old man Willie Umprey on the clarinet. Uh-huh. Now, at that time, they didn't allow no, uh, blowing instruments in the district there. Oh, yeah. I'm the first man that put the blowing instruments there.
